n: Peter, the senior Apostle, writes to believers spread across five Roman provinces in what is now Turkey. He calls them “strangers”—people whose true home is with God.

f.g: Temporary residents, exiles living away from home.

f.w: Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia
f.g: Roman provinces in Asia Minor (modern Turkey).

n: These Saints were chosen in God’s plan, made holy by the Spirit, and called to obey Christ and be cleansed by His blood. All three members of the Godhead are named.

f.g: Echoes covenant rites where blood was sprinkled on the people.

n: Peter bursts into praise: in His great mercy God has given us a new birth into a living hope, made possible because Jesus rose from the dead.

f.g: Born again; given new spiritual life.
lively = living.

n: That hope is an inheritance that can’t decay, be stained, or fade—kept safe in heaven for you.
And you yourselves are guarded by God’s power through your faith until the full salvation is revealed at the end.

f.g: Guarded, as by a military garrison.

n: This hope brings deep joy, even though for a little while you may be weighed down by many kinds of trials.

f.g: Grief, sorrow.
Many kinds of trials.

n: Gold is refined by fire, yet gold eventually perishes. Your tested faith is far more precious, and it will bring praise and glory when Jesus Christ appears.
Though you have never seen Jesus, you love Him and believe in Him, and you are filled with a joy too glorious for words.
The result of your faith is the salvation of your souls.

f.g: The goal or outcome of faith.

n: Ancient prophets searched carefully about this salvation and the grace that would come to you.
The Spirit of Christ in those prophets testified in advance of Christ’s sufferings and the glory afterward. Latter-day Saints see this fulfilled in Book of Mormon prophets too.
The prophets knew they were serving future generations. The same message has now been preached to you by the Holy Ghost—truths even angels long to understand.

f.g: To stoop and peer into, as if leaning to see more clearly.

n: So get your minds ready for action, stay clear-headed, and set your hope fully on the grace you will receive when Jesus Christ is revealed.

f.w: gird up the loins of your mind
f.g: Tuck up your long robe to move freely—be mentally prepared.
Self-controlled, alert.

n: Be like obedient children and don’t shape your lives around the desires you followed before you knew the gospel.

f.g: Conforming, molding yourselves.

n: Since the God who called you is holy, become holy in every part of your conduct.

f.g: Conduct, way of life.

n: Peter quotes the command God gave Israel: be holy, because I am holy.
If you call on a Father who judges everyone fairly by their deeds, then live your time here on earth with reverence.

f.g: Temporary stay, as a foreigner.
Reverent awe, not terror.

n: You were rescued from the empty lifestyle passed down by your ancestors—not with silver or gold, which wear out.

f.g: Bought back, ransomed, as from slavery.
Empty way of life.

n: Instead, you were redeemed by Christ’s precious blood, like a flawless Passover lamb. His sacrifice is the price of our freedom.
Christ was chosen for this mission before the world was created, but He has come in these last times for your sake. Latter-day Saints connect this to the premortal council.

f.w: foreordained before the foundation of the world

n: Through Christ you believe in the God who raised Him from the dead and glorified Him, so your faith and hope rest in God.

f.w: raised him up from the dead

n: Having cleansed your souls by obeying the truth, you now have sincere love for fellow believers. So love one another deeply, from a pure heart.

f.g: Sincere, not pretended.
Intensely, stretched out to the full.

n: You have been born again from a seed that can’t die—the living and lasting word of God.
Peter quotes Isaiah: people and their glory are like grass and wildflowers that wither and fall.
But the Lord’s word lasts forever—and that enduring word is the very gospel that was preached to you.
